_note: Per-line decomposition of the streams that `s12-session-config.json` declares as shared. Allowed identities per line are exactly the ones the config declares for that mic, plus `NPC:<Name>` when the mic carries the GM. Segment text must be a verbatim substring of the raw indexed line. This file records semantic decisions made while reading the raw lines — it never declares WHICH mics are shared; that is the user-provided config's job. Full-stream audit: every Luke S line carries an explicit decision; `ooc: true` marks out-of-character table talk (Tier C).
_ooc_note: Out-of-character is a fact about the TABLE, not about one microphone: when the group is talking about Wi-Fi, character sheets or how good the session was, every stream is the person speaking, not their character. `ooc_ranges` and `ooc_lines` therefore apply to all streams, and the renderer labels anything they cover with the PERSON's name. Criterion used while reading the raw: real-world/table/meta content (tech, rules, campaign praise, scheduling, discussion of the GM's NPC voices) is out of character; a player narrating their own character's action in the third person is still play and keeps the character label. Boundaries were read off the raw lines, never inferred from a keyword.
